germany.name: Germany
germany.intro: Germany runs 19% standard VAT with mandatory OSS for cross-border B2C above €10,000. EPR registration is centralized through LUCID (Verpackungsregister) with separate streams for packaging, batteries, and WEEE. UStG, VerpackG, and GwG are the primary statutes you will encounter.
cover: VAT registration · OSS / IOSS quarterly returns
matters: You ship physical goods into Germany
Your cross-border B2C revenue crosses €10,000
You join Amazon FBA-DE or a German marketplace

unitedKingdom.name: United Kingdom
unitedKingdom.regime: UK VAT · Packaging EPR · WEEE · PPT
unitedKingdom.intro: Post-Brexit, the UK sits outside the EU OSS. You register for UK VAT once you sell to UK consumers, with marketplaces often the deemed supplier. Packaging EPR and WEEE run through national schemes, separate from any EU registration.
matters: You sell to UK consumers post-Brexit
You import goods into Great Britain
You place packaging on the UK market

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.intro: The Netherlands applies standard EU VAT with OSS for cross-border B2C. Producer responsibility covers packaging (Afvalfonds / UPV), electronics (WEEE), and batteries — each with its own registration and reporting cadence.
matters: You sell B2C into the Netherlands
You ship packaged goods to NL consumers
You hold stock in a Dutch warehouse

france.name: France
france.intro: France runs EU VAT with OSS and one of the broadest EPR regimes under the AGEC law — packaging, electronics, furniture, textiles and more, each with a unique identifier (IDU) and eco-organisme. Ecomodulation and repairability scores increasingly apply.
matters: You sell B2C into France
You place packaging or EEE on the French market
You sell textiles, furniture or toys to FR consumers

italy.name: Italy
italy.intro: Italy applies EU VAT with OSS and mandatory e-invoicing (SdI) for many flows. Packaging EPR runs through CONAI with environmental-labelling obligations, while REACH applies to chemical content in goods.
matters: You sell B2C into Italy
You place packaging on the Italian market
You ship products with regulated chemical content

spain.name: Spain
spain.intro: Spain runs EU VAT with OSS and has expanded packaging EPR under Royal Decree 1055/2022, including a plastic-packaging tax. Ecodesign and SCIP obligations apply to many product categories.
matters: You sell B2C into Spain
You place plastic packaging on the Spanish market
You ship EEE or regulated products to ES

unitedStates.name: United States
unitedStates.intro: The US has no VAT; state-level sales tax applies once you cross economic nexus thresholds (often $100k or 200 transactions per state). Marketplace facilitator laws shift collection to platforms in most states.
matters: You sell to US consumers across states
You cross a state economic-nexus threshold
You sell on a US marketplace

turkiye.name: Türkiye
turkiye.intro: Türkiye applies KDV (VAT) with mandatory e-invoicing (e-Fatura) and e-archive (e-Arşiv) for many taxpayers. Cross-border digital and goods flows carry their own registration and withholding rules, with FX in TRY.
matters: You sell to Turkish consumers
You issue invoices subject to e-Fatura
You provide digital services into Türkiye

items.title: EPR & Packaging
items.desc: Know whether you count as a producer in a market — and what you must register before the first shipment.
items.intro:
Sell physical products online? EPR and packaging requirements may apply—even if you did not manufacture the products. Find out which registrations and other steps may be required in each market.

Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and packaging rules can apply when you sell or ship physical products into a country, including through an online marketplace or your own website. Depending on the market and product category, you may need to register, report volumes, contribute to recycling costs, meet take-back obligations, or appoint an authorized representative.
matters: You sell or ship physical products through a marketplace, your own website, or another sales channel.

terms.tip: Rules that place responsibility for a product’s end-of-life environmental impact on certain businesses.
Rules covering waste electrical and electronic equipment.
Fees adjusted according to environmental characteristics such as recyclability or material use.

items.q: Is the assessment free?
items.a: Yes. You can complete the assessment and view your Risk Map without an account or payment. A free account lets you save and update your Risk Map, see your best matches, book consultations, and receive available alerts.

items.q: How personalized is my Risk Map?
items.a: Your Risk Map is based on the markets, business model, products or services, activities, and areas of support you select. The more complete your answers are, the more relevant the results can be. We will identify when more information is needed.

items.q: What if I am unsure about an answer?
items.a: You can skip questions you are unsure about, return to them later, or request professional support when confirmation is needed.

items.q: What do the Risk Map statuses mean?
items.a: Confirmed means the requirement applies based on your answers. Likely to Apply means it probably applies, but more information or professional confirmation may be needed. More Information Needed means additional answers are required for a more accurate assessment.

items.q: Where does the information come from?
items.a: Regulatory information is based on official authority sources. Where available, we show the authority, source link, relevant date, and when the information was last reviewed.

items.q: Can I assess several markets or areas at once?
items.a: Yes. You can include multiple markets and areas of support in one organized Risk Map.

items.q: Can I change my answers or update my Risk Map?
items.a: Yes. Update your answers when your activities, markets, products, or business structure change.

items.q: Can I export my information?
items.a: You can export your Risk Map as a PDF. Depending on availability and your account features, engagement records may also be available as PDF, CSV, or through an API.

items.q: What if my market is not available?
items.a: You can request an additional market and, where available, choose to receive an alert when coverage becomes available.

items.q: Does CompliHub360 provide legal, tax, accounting, or other professional advice?
items.a: No. CompliHub360 provides compliance information and matching services. We are not a law firm, accounting firm, tax adviser, customs broker, or regulatory authority. Advice and professional services are provided independently by the selected provider.

items.q: How are providers reviewed?
items.a: Providers are reviewed against applicable criteria such as qualifications, expertise, market coverage, business information, experience, and service standards. Where available, we may also verify licenses, certifications, response history, reviews, and completed engagements.

items.q: Why are provider names hidden at first?
items.a: Provider names remain hidden during the initial comparison so you can focus on expertise and fit rather than brand recognition. This also gives providers of different sizes a fair opportunity to be selected.

items.q: When will I see the provider’s name and full profile?
items.a: The provider’s identity and full profile are revealed after you choose the provider and book a consultation. You can then review its verified credentials, reviews, business-verification information, and contact details.

items.q: Can providers pay to appear higher in my matches?
items.a: No. Matching and ranking are based on relevant criteria and cannot be purchased. Advertising budgets, brand size, and commercial arrangements do not determine your best matches.

items.q: How much will the service cost?
items.a: You see an expected price range before choosing a provider. After the consultation, the provider confirms the services, final price, expected timeline, and terms. Professional work begins only after you approve them.

items.q: How quickly will a provider respond?
items.a: The provider’s expected response time is shown before you choose. If the provider does not respond within that period, CompliHub360 can suggest another match. Your information will not be shared with another provider without your approval.

items.q: Can I choose more than one provider?
items.a: Yes. You can select and book consultations with more than one provider. Each booking and professional engagement remains separate.

items.q: What happens after I book?
items.a: The provider’s identity and full profile are revealed, and only the information needed to process your request is shared. The provider then confirms the service, price, timeline, and terms. No professional work begins until you approve it.

items.q: Am I required to continue with the provider after the consultation?
items.a: No. Booking a consultation does not require you to begin a professional engagement.

items.q: How does CompliHub360 support free access for users?
items.a: CompliHub360 is free for businesses seeking support. We earn revenue through our commercial relationships with participating providers. These arrangements never influence which providers appear in your matches or how they are ranked.

items.q: Do I need an account?
items.a: No account is required to ask a question, complete the assessment, or view your initial Risk Map. A free account is required to save and update results, see your best matches, book consultations, and use available workspace features.

items.q: How is my information used?
items.a: We use your information to provide the services you request, personalize relevant results, operate your account, and support the matching and booking process, as explained in our Privacy Policy.

items.q: What information is shared with a provider?
items.a: If you choose to connect or book, we share only the information needed to process your request. You should be shown what will be shared before the connection is completed.

items.q: When is my information shared?
items.a: Your information is shared after you choose to connect or book with a provider and complete the relevant confirmation step. It is not automatically shared with every provider shown in your matches.

items.q: Does CompliHub360 sell my personal or business information?
items.a:
No. CompliHub360 does not sell your personal or business information to unrelated third parties.

If you choose to connect or book with a service provider, we share only the information needed to process your request, as explained in our Privacy Policy.

items.q: How is my information protected?
items.a: We use appropriate technical and organizational measures designed to protect personal and business information. Additional details are provided in our Privacy Policy and security information.

items.q: Can I control notifications?
items.a: Yes. Where notification features are available, you can manage your email and regulatory-alert preferences from your account or use the unsubscribe option provided in the message.

items.q: Can I delete my account or request deletion of my information?
items.a: You can request account deletion and exercise applicable privacy rights as explained in our Privacy Policy. Some information may need to be retained where required by law or for legitimate recordkeeping purposes.

items.q: Where is my information stored?
items.a: Information is stored and processed through service providers and locations described in our Privacy Policy. Applicable safeguards are used where information is transferred between countries.

tips.completedEngagements: Professional engagements recorded as completed through CompliHub360.
tips.identity: The provider’s name and full profile are shown after you select the provider and book a consultation.
tips.officialSource: The authority’s own publication, such as a law, regulation, or official guidance, linked where it is available online.
tips.priority: How soon a requirement needs your attention, from Immediate to Low, based on its deadline and its consequences.

status.confirmed: This requirement applies based on the information you provided.
status.likely: This requirement probably applies, but additional information or professional confirmation may be needed.
status.moreInfo: Answer a few additional questions so we can assess this requirement more accurately.
